title: What does MPTokenIssuanceSet do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of MPTokenIssuanceSet and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, MPTokenIssuanceSet changes the mutable properties or holder controls of an existing MPT issuance. [1]

The issuer's original capabilities limit which changes are allowed. Locking behavior and authorization are distinct from changing the asset's identity. Inspect whether the operation targets the whole issuance or a specific holder. A mutable setting cannot be assumed to override a capability that was deliberately absent at creation. [1]

The MPTokenIssuanceSet reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using MPTokenIssuanceSet, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
